scope: Read-only research on specializing only the immutable bundled default Noto Sans, preserving arbitrary caller fonts, raw-count audit, and resource-handle alternatives. No repo files or shared worktrees were changed; no compiler or timing experiments were run.

verified_local_facts.fact: The shipped primary font is Noto Sans 2.015, source hash bfb7bb691513f12e734dc346c03a03f784912432d7e3fa8e56efcf906fe86b3d, 2,049,096 bytes. Its fvar defaults are wght=400 and wdth=100; source README says unmodified and preserves Google Fonts commit 2984c575fdce412ee02b2baaba67672b9a9434d8.

The isolated fontTools 4.67.0 prototype is 646,160 bytes (saving 1,402,936 bytes, 68.46% of this asset), SHA-256 16a1ee5229882c1ba577d265014a85d8a4ddbcf5e45bd30bcfbabfdaf89cabf3. It retains 4,515 glyphs in the same order. This is file-payload evidence only; its own result scope expressly says no shaping, outline, pixel, RSS, startup or adoption result.

Table sizes changed: GPOS 243,810→127,538; GSUB 72,970→83,226; GDEF 30,169→1,738; HVAR 21,207→0; MVAR 130→0; avar 68→0; fvar 182→0; gvar 1,245,578→0. Glyf changed 326,949→326,951 bytes; hmtx/cmap/hhea/head/maxp/hinting table lengths are unchanged in this prototype. A rewrite and matching size are not behavioral proof.

The current exact Unicode certificate is derived from all three bundled cmaps and asserts exact glyph-zero/nonzero coverage across every Unicode scalar; the output font still needs to be used as input when regenerating and verifying the certificate. Equal glyph order alone does not prove an unchanged cmap mapping.

The primary bundled font and caller fonts share FontFace::new/from_data behavior; custom fonts are owned once, and layouts own FontSet/FontFace leases. The current register_font metadata passes axes=[('wght',400)] for every face. Fontique documents this field as default values for variation axes. Treat this as a review point for custom fonts with a non-400 wght default; specialize only the bundled primary, and test any change against the existing custom default-instance test before altering behavior.

verified_local_facts.fact: The raw count getter sums glyph_len on the line-scoped ShapedSlice. Inline glyphs are defined to have glyph_len=1; newlines can have zero glyphs. Positioned glyph iteration traverses those same shaped clusters and inline/stored representations. Existing source tests check equality on wraps, script mixes, bidi controls, spaces, empty content and a 512-mark grapheme. This is strong local evidence, with no remaining count gap found in the inspected APIs; parent reports the committed negative +1 fault control and cross-platform/fallback checks separately.

FontFace is already one pointer word (8 bytes on x86_64). Existing lifecycle tests require concurrent bundled acquisition to mint once, identity equality while live, a returned layout to retain that exact face, no identity after its final owner drops, a strictly newer ID on remint, poison recovery, and Send+Sync. Separate equal caller bytes intentionally create a different identity; foreign layouts must be rejected. Fallback layouts also retain FontSet leases.

The asset license is SIL OFL 1.1. The bundled copy contains attribution plus the license; the license allows modification and bundling subject to keeping the font under OFL and the reserved-name condition. The current OFL file has no 'with Reserved Font Name' text in its copyright header. Update asset README to say derived static instance and preserve provenance/license when adopting. Host Fontconfig reports the candidate as Noto Sans Regular; that metadata check is not a license review.

verified_spec_facts: At an axis default, the base glyf outline and other default table values define the default instance; deltas are for non-default variation. However a whole font instance includes much more than glyf: metric tables, layout positioning and substitutions, caret/anchor data and other table values may vary.

TrueType phantom points in gvar affect advances and side bearings; HVAR is a separate efficient metrics mechanism. MVAR adjusts font-wide metrics. GDEF's ItemVariationStore can adjust GDEF/GPOS/JSTF values, including caret and positioning-related data. GSUB and GPOS FeatureVariations can replace lookups in axis regions.

The OpenType spec allows precision differences when generating a static font from an instance and explicitly warns that minor differences can result. Default outline equivalence therefore does not imply exact serialized coordinates or pixel identity.
less_obvious_fontTools_4_67_checks: The 4.67.0 release notes call out applying VVAR vertical-origin deltas to VORG and OpenType rounding for instanced advances/origins; universal FeatureVariations records after pinning; preservation of ppem Device corrections in GDEF/BASE/GPOS/JSTF; MATH VariationIndex folding/remapping; FeatureVariation record/offset/order fixes. Inspect which structures actually occur in this Noto font, but include these as regression targets because the candidate rewrote GSUB/GPOS/GDEF and the converter version is exactly 4.67.0.

Check that default normalized coordinate zero is handled exactly with avar normalization, variable-to-static table rewriting, and feature condition comparisons. OpenType requires exact 2.14 normalized values for FeatureVariation conditions and TrueType GET VARIATION; the default maps to zero, but the converter path and chosen axis values must be pinned and reproducible.

Check simple and composite TrueType glyphs, inferred gvar point deltas, phantom points, implied on-curve points, composite component placement, and integer coordinate rounding; fontTools output's glyf length changes by two bytes even though the instance should be the default.

Compare font-wide metrics including OS/2 typo/win metrics, hhea, post underline values and gasp; hmtx equality alone misses MVAR-derived deltas. Compare GDEF caret values and GPOS mark/cursive attachment/kerning; no claim that existing Canvas exercises all of these is established.

Inspect Device tables and FeatureVariations in source and candidate, and test actual output at representative ppem/font sizes. Existing Canvas rasterization is unhinted; font shaping and GDEF caret/layout code can still make other table values observable.
recommended_executable_proof_before_ship: Freeze provenance: verify source SHA, wheel SHA (4304f03ed7f4ba000a8dcc941ad854bfa52e2f3b6112b8f099b6f431cf98e701), exact command/options, output SHA and license note in an isolated reproducible regeneration script. The current wheel URL is https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/3d/61/4161946319472aaa9b897bd18ad5108a5b10f5ebaa503d921a001ac4fff9/fonttools-4.67.0-py3-none-any.whl.

Run an independent parser/validator (for example OpenType Sanitizer plus a different runtime parser) on source and output. Compare every scalar's exact cmap GID, all 4,515 names/order, glyph count, hmtx advances/LSBs, hhea/OS2/head metrics, glyf bounds/contours/points and all non-variation tables after expected staticization. Regenerate font-coverage.bin from the candidate cmap and run the existing exhaustive scalar certificate test.

Use an independent shaping engine (Rustybuzz/HarfBuzz) with source variable font set to both exact axis defaults and candidate static font; compare glyph IDs, clusters, advances, offsets, direction, and fallback choice. Include Latin kerning/ligatures, Greek/Cyrillic, Hebrew/Arabic marks and cursive shaping, Indic combining marks if supported, variation selectors/default ignorables, long mark stacks, paragraphs/wraps, caret endpoints and ligature carets. Keep the existing custom caller-supplied variable-font default-instance regression unchanged as a boundary control.

Run actual Canvas static-candidate corpus through current Parley/Skrifa and Swash and compare layout geometry, ink bounds, raster mask dimensions, placement and coverage against original variable-font default. Require the current chosen tolerances to be explicit; do not require byte identity if approved outline rounding changes, but ensure script and fallback semantics remain equal. Add scripts using output font and assert bundle's immutable coverage asset matches it exactly.

After correctness gates, measure package/file bytes separately from runtime resident pages in fresh processes. Record RSS and touched-page/page-fault behavior under no-shape, ASCII shape, extended Unicode and mark-heavy workloads; do not claim 1.4MB RSS relief from the 1.4MB smaller asset. Build-time executable size and runtime resident set are distinct observables.
adversarial_font_specialization_audit.verified_inference_boundary: No independent shaping, outlines, pixels, metrics, cmap equality, certificate regeneration, or RSS test was run by this researcher. The savings, hashes, table lengths and glyph-order equality are directly reported by the isolated prototype; possible behavioral parity is a hypothesis requiring the controls above.

contract_bill: An owned FontFace and any TextLayout that names it must keep the exact immutable resource live until the last lease drops.
While any owner remains, bundled() must return the exact same identity; after all FontFace, TextSystem, fallback and layout owners are gone, a later bundled() must mint a distinct higher ID.

Cold concurrent initialization must publish exactly one complete valid identity, recover from poison, and preserve Send+Sync. Caller Arc-backed faces keep their current owned bytes and separate identity even when byte-equal to the bundled asset.
resource_handle_recommendation.assessment: Keep std::sync::Arc/Weak unless an isolated implementation proves a measured benefit. ArcBorrow is a copyable non-owning borrow, so it cannot itself preserve the owned TextLayout lease or weak release/remint semantics. Triomphe ArcBorrow is similarly borrowed; triomphe Arc documents no Weak references. A safe registry-index handle can remain one word but introduces clone/drop table synchronization and generation accounting. A one-word raw tagged Arc/static pointer needs manual strong-count/drop handling or pointer tagging, which is unsafe and conflicts with crates/canvas/src/lib.rs#![forbid(unsafe_code)]. The current 8-byte FontFace already matches pointer width; no demonstrated layout-header reduction is available. Static bytes are already immortal arrays; the dynamic FontData/Arc currently provides lifecycle identity and leases, not the 2MB byte payload copy.
resource_handle_recommendation.possible_narrow_experiment: If profiling later shows admission is material, first prototype an isolated safe bundled-token/refcount design without changing custom Arc faces. Count registry locks, clone/drop atomics, cold parsing, per-face FontData/control-block allocations, retained bytes and contention. Preserve exact existing tests before considering an implementation; do not treat immortal generation IDs as equivalent to current remint identity.

raw_count_audit.reasoning: The stored glyph backing is an indexed concatenation of each shaped cluster's glyph run. Inline storage is used only for a single glyph and reports glyph_len 1; multi-glyph stored clusters report their full count; no-glyph/newline clusters report 0. Line-scoped Run uses the same shaped cluster range narrowed to that line. Positioning iterators yield each such cluster glyph exactly once; spacing changes coordinates/advances, not iterator cardinality. Thus summing lengths preserves the count while avoiding construction of positioned Glyph values and spacing work.
raw_count_audit.potential_limit: The local equality corpus is broad for structural edge cases but does not enumerate all Unicode or every custom shaper/font. The method depends on Parley's cluster invariant; keep a focused conservation oracle on upstream/vendor changes. The sum uses usize with iterator sum; on ordinary 64-bit targets MAX_TEXT/MAX_GLYPHS dominate, while theoretical adversarial overflow on a 32-bit target merits a checked sum only if such a target is in product scope.
